subject: BriskWare connector: production latency spike — coordination on support bridge & SLA fallback
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moran <alex.moran@briskware.io>; partnerships@briskware.io
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BriskWare connector: production latency spike — coordination on support bridge & SLA fallback

Alex / Partnerships —

Heads up: starting ~08:50 PT this morning we've seen a repeated pattern of elevated latency and intermittent 5xxs for customer webhooks routed through the BriskWare connector (multiple accounts across us-west). Symptoms: tokenization timeouts, backlog on the async worker, and occasional double-delivery attempts from our side. Impact is limited to ~15% of requests but is causing elevated error budgets for customers on Dedicated + Hosted.

Attached I've dropped a small log bundle (support_snapshot.tar.gz) with trace ids and a short timeline. Can we spin up a short triage bridge (30 mins) to align on immediate mitigations and an interim SLA fallback (route to the Dedicated-compatible variant or enable short-circuiting) while we investigate root cause?

Primary asks:
- Confirm best escalation contact at BriskWare reachable for an on-call bridge within the hour.
- Agree temporary routing/fallback plan and how long BriskWare will own remediation versus Redwood applying a routing override.
- Collect any early indicators from BriskWare (deploys, infra events) that might explain the spike.

Sergio / Jonas — looping you for ops + partner coordination. If we need to apply an emergency routing override on Redwood side I want engineering sign-off.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Partnerships — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: support_snapshot.tar.gz (log bundle, 3.2MB)
From: Alex Moran <alex.moran@briskware.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: partnerships@briskware.io; Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BriskWare connector: production latency spike — coordination on support bridge & SLA fallback

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick flag and the log bundle. We're seeing related error traces on our side starting ~08:45 PT that look like a downstream cache saturation combined with a malformed rate limiter rule in a recent canary. We're pulling the artifacts now.

I can be on a bridge in 20 minutes. Our primary on-call for this area is Tim Hale (cc'd) and partnerships@briskware.io; Tim is reachable at +1 206-555-0444.

Short-term we can:
- Disable the new rate limiter canary (5–10 min rollback) — probable fastest mitigation.
- Throttle problematic source IP ranges for 30m as a stopgap.

We agree a temporary routing fallback is sensible — if Redwood can route traffic to the Dedicated-compatible variant and mark BriskWare as primary-owner for remediation, that balances risk. We'll prepare a rollback patch and a short runbook. I'll upload that immediately to the shared folder.

—Alex
Alex Moran
Head of Integrations — BriskWare
alex.moran@briskware.io

Attachment: none
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Moran <alex.moran@briskware.io>; partnerships@briskware.io
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BriskWare connector: production latency spike — coordination on support bridge & SLA fallback

All —

I'll take ownership of the partner coordination on the bridge. Proposed immediate plan (agree / call now if objections):

1) Start a 30-minute bridge at 09:40 PT. Sergio (me) + Jonas (runtime) + Marissa + Alex + Tim.
2) Redwood will stand up an emergency routing override to send new traffic to the Dedicated-compatible connector if latency > 800ms for 5 consecutive minutes. This will be limited to the affected accounts list (we'll share).
3) BriskWare will perform an emergency rollback of the canary; if rollback takes > 20 minutes we'll keep the routing override until verified green.
4) Post-incident: joint postmortem and an SLA addendum clause for connector canaries and rate-limiter changes — propose 4-hour on-call response for P1s, 24-hour remediation for operational fixes, and a defined rollback playbook.

Jonas — can you prepare the routing override and escalation_contacts.csv with phone numbers for our ops team? I will start the bridge invite.

Sergio Alvarez
Strategic Partnerships — Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachment: none
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Moran <alex.moran@briskware.io>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BriskWare connector: production latency spike — coordination on support bridge & SLA fallback

On it — ops team standing by. I've attached a short-runbook draft (proposed_runbook_v1.md) that covers immediate rollback steps, verification queries (trace ids to confirm pathing), and how to toggle Redwood's routing override.

I'll be on the bridge and will have the emergency routing toggle ready as a one-click job; target time to flip is ~2 minutes once authorized. Also attaching escalation_contacts.csv (internal + BriskWare on-call numbers).

If we do the routing override: note that some customers with pinned model versions may see tokenization time change; we'll include a short customer-facing note after we stabilize.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
SRE — Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

Attachment: proposed_runbook_v1.md; escalation_contacts.csv
From: Alex Moran <alex.moran@briskware.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: partnerships@briskware.io; Tim Hale <timothy.hale@cloudforge.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BriskWare connector: production latency spike — coordination on support bridge & SLA fallback

Confirming outcome from the bridge / follow-ups:

- Root cause: canaryed rate-limiter + cache boundary condition. Canary rollback completed at 09:58 PT; traffic returned to baseline by 10:06 PT.
- BriskWare will add an automated canary kill-switch for future rate-limiter changes and provide a short changelog for any infra canary deployments touching production.
- Agreed interim SLA: 4-hour on-call response for P1s and a 24-hour remediation expectation for operational config fixes. We will follow up with formal language for the partnership agreement.
- Shared postmortem and runbook uploaded: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/partnerships/BriskWare/postmortem-20260814

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination. We'll wait for the formalized SLA addendum and the BriskWare changelog before closing.

—Alex
Alex Moran
Head of Integrations — BriskWare

Attachment: none
